This role modifies a live serverless gateway in production - no downtime, no change in behaviour - leaving a clean handoff point for a downstream build managed in Terraform. This is careful surgery on production infrastructure with active external consumers, not a greenfield build.
The scope includes modernizing a CDK estate made up of four stacks, six Lambda functions, a WAF web ACL, an mTLS custom domain/truststore, and a REST API - preserving resource identity during consolidation and coordinating two sequenced deployments with a tested rollback path.
What you will do

• Inventory the CDK estate and build a modernization plan: upgrade the CDK library/CLI, replace deprecated constructs, move hardcoded context into per-environment config.

• Consolidate duplicated stacks into shared constructs without losing resource identity - map logical IDs before and after, pick a preservation method, and confirm nothing gets replaced before touching production.

• Run the library upgrade and the stack refactor as two separate, ordered deployments, with a rollback path tested in dev and test first.

• Migrate all six Lambda functions from Node 18 to Node 24, close an open PII logging finding, and regression-test each one.

• Re-verify the security perimeter after both deployments - WAF, the mTLS domain and truststore, X-Ray tracing, upstream timeouts - working directly with the customer's POS team across all six external callers.

• Build deployment pipelines for dev/test/prod with OIDC federation, approval gates, and a ServiceNow change step. Add CDK assertion tests, drift detection, and API access log retention.

• Publish the SQS queue ARN and KMS key ARN via Parameter Store, and grant send permission to the downstream Terraform-managed system - this is the key ordering dependency for that team's build.

• Align naming, tagging, and documentation with the customer's internal standards, and document your identity-preservation decisions clearly enough for the next engineer to follow.

About the role

NETGEAR is building an in-house creative team to own campaign, web, and social work end to end. The team is small on purpose: a Creative Lead, a UI Designer, a Graphic Designer, and a copywriter.

This work supports the Consumer-facing side of NETGEAR. You will be the main person responsible for execution and production across what the team makes: web assets, social, paid ads, campaign work, email templates, retail signage, and event booth graphics. In a given month you might move from a paid social set to a booth graphic to a product landing page.

Everything runs to established NETGEAR brand guidelines. The craft is in making distinctive work within those rules rather than around them.

You will also work with the Creative Lead on campaign concepts and help shape where the brand goes next. We are looking for someone who brings ideas, not only someone who executes them well.

What you will do

- Design assets across web, social, paid ads, email templates, campaign work, retail signage, event graphics, and sales collateral, working from briefs and alongside the UI Designer and Creative Lead.

- Contribute creative ideas. Bring concepts into campaign discussions with the Creative Lead, and propose directions of your own.

- Adapt campaign concepts into full asset sets across formats, sizes, and channels.

- Work to NETGEAR brand guidelines across everything you produce, applying them consistently and helping extend the system as new needs come up.

- Prepare and hand off production-ready files for both screen and print.

- Use AI tools as a working part of your process, for ideation, iteration, and production. Fluency is welcome, but a genuine interest in the tools and a willingness to build them into how you work matters more. What we do expect is the judgment to recognize when AI output falls short of the standard required and needs to be reworked by hand.

- Collaborate directly with project stakeholders across marketing, product, and web, and incorporate their feedback into revisions.

- Work closely with our Sr. Integrated Marketing Manager, who is responsible for global campaigns, so that what you produce fits the wider campaign plan.

What we are looking for

- 4+ years of professional graphic design experience, ideally in-house or brand-side. Consumer tech, DTC, or ecommerce experience is a strong plus.

- A portfolio showing volume and range, not just showpiece work. We want to see campaign systems, social sets, and web assets, and hear what the constraints were.

- Strong fluency in Figma. Most of our digital assets are designed there, so this is the tool you will spend most of your time in. Solid Adobe Creative Cloud skills alongside it.

- Strong interest in AI, backed by practical experience using it in a design workflow. You should be following how the tools are developing, testing new ones as they appear rather than reading about them, and bringing back what actually works.

- A sharp eye for detail. Spacing, alignment, typography, and colour handled precisely, and errors caught before they reach a stakeholder or a printer.

- Ideas of your own. We want to see concept thinking in your portfolio, not only well-executed versions of someone else’s direction.

- Comfortable working to an existing brand system rather than reinventing one per project.

- A positive, curious attitude and a real appetite for learning. We support training on new tools, AI in particular.

- Reliable under a queue. You can hold several projects at different stages and keep the status visible without being chased.

Nice to have

Job Description:

The Product Specialist is an entry-level product support and enablement role. This role builds product knowledge, supports internal teams with repeatable product questions, helps maintain product documentation, and supports self-service resources. The goal is to help internal teams find clear, accurate, and current product information across assigned product lines.
The Product Specialist works under the guidance of Product Management. This role supports product education, inquiry support, documentation updates, release awareness, and internal enablement. The role does not make final product decisions, set roadmap priorities, or own product strategy. It helps Product Management see recurring questions, documentation gaps, training needs, and ways to make product guidance easier for internal teams to use.

Key Responsibilities:

•
Product learning and release awareness: Build working knowledge of assigned product lines, including product features, workflows, common use cases, customer scenarios, support paths, and release changes. Stay current by attending product show-and-tell sessions, release reviews, training sessions, enablement sessions, and product demos. Review release notes, Product Hub updates, internal documentation, and other available resources to keep learning and identify knowledge gaps.

•
Internal product inquiry support: Support repeatable product, workflow, configuration, and process questions that belong with Product. Provide clear, consistent, and timely guidance to internal teams within defined response-time expectations or service level agreements. Help prepare client-facing response language or talking points for review when needed, and help guide teams to the right next step.

•
Documentation, Product Hub, and Accurate Ally validation: Help create, update, and maintain Product Hub content, FAQs, user guides, troubleshooting documentation, and workflow guidance,. Make sure content is accurate, easy to understand, easy to find, and useful for self-service. When Product Hub content is updated, test Accurate Ally to confirm it can read the updated content and return clear, accurate, and helpful answers based on approved guidance.

•
Inquiry tracking and escalation support: Track product inquiries by source, type, product area, resolution path, escalation owner, and documentation opportunity. Route misdirected questions to the right owner. Escalate to Product Management when product decisions, roadmap context, client-specific exceptions, or strategic input are needed. Include clear context, business impact, steps already taken, and a recommended next step when escalating.

•
Cross-functional collaboration and enablement support: Work with Sales, Account Management, Solutions, Operations, Support, App Support, Implementation, Compliance, Engineering, vendors, and other internal teams to clarify product guidance. Identify training opportunities, enablement gaps, and areas where teams need clearer support. When approved, help close those gaps through documentation updates, training support, office hours, or other enablement resources under Product Management direction.

•
Theme identification and feedback to Product Management: Identify recurring questions, customer pain points, documentation gaps, misdirected inquiries, and common support themes. Summarize patterns and observations for Product Management so they can guide documentation updates, enablement priorities, support improvements, and future product discussions.

•
Serve as a Product SME for Sales and Account Management teams: support customer meetings, product discussions, and demonstrations as needed.
